cells.tense: You are moving now, with the pen, from what you actually feel.
cells.ask: Tell one person where you're headed and the next single step — out loud, today, no pitch attached.
cells.core: You're moving, and it's coming from what you actually feel rather than from pressure. When something matters to you the energy follows it, so you don't have to force yourself into gear. You hold a direction through resistance without getting eaten by it, and that's the part most people lose first. In this stretch it's holding.\n\nWhat it can feed next is a picture of the step after this one. Not a five-year plan — just enough imagination to see past the thing you're already on. Aim high, keep the next move small. When it's working you can name where you're going and take one step toward it without needing the whole road lit. That's the version to keep feeding.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving from what you feel, and it's carrying you.
cells.verb: Keeping your energy pointed at a destination until it's reached
cells.place: the stretch where feeling turns into a direction you can move in

cells.tense: You are already living past the destination, bracing for a future you can't write in.
cells.ask: Pick the thing that's actually finished and stop pushing on it. Say it's done out loud, tonight, to one person. Don't start the next one before you sleep.
cells.core: You're ahead of yourself. One thing gets close to done and you're already on the next, so the goal that was supposed to be the finish line keeps sliding out of reach. The drive is real. It's just running past what it was aiming at, and you don't get to feel the win because you don't stop long enough for it to land.\n\nWhat helps here is checking, honestly, whether the thing you're still forcing is already finished. That's the difference between adding and subtracting — know which one you're doing. When you can feel this is done, this is next, the motion has a shape again. Ask someone close which one they see you still pushing. Their answer is the trim.
cells.sheetLine: You're driving past the finish line and calling it progress.

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that is already behind you, and you are still standing there.
cells.ask: Close one open loop today — say the ending out loud to yourself, then to one person. Let the cleared space sit for a week before you fill it.
cells.core: There's feeling, and there's no forward motion. You know what you want and it doesn't turn into a step, and the longer it sits the more the not-doing starts to look like the truth about you. It isn't. There's no push in you right now to move on this, and pushing harder just spends what little is there.\n\nWhen this is working, feeling turns into a direction and then into one step — the two on the same track, and the step arrives because you decided to take it. What refills it is finishing something: one honest ending, letting what's over be over. When that closes, movement starts coming back by itself. The step after will be small. Take it anyway.

cells.tense: You are steering right now without your hand on the wheel, in a room you're already moving through.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today and say "I did that" — out loud, no qualifier, no 'we'. Then do the same thing tomorrow on purpose.
cells.core: You're moving something forward right now and telling yourself it's just happening. Plans you're shaping, decisions you're making — you call it the situation, the timing, the way things went. The direction is yours. The account you give of it leaves you out. The same thing shows up the other way too: a stuck spot you can't see as stuck, because you've stopped noticing the wheel at all.\n\nWhat returns it is small and specific. Pick one thing that moved today because you moved it, and say so plainly — to yourself first. The story that says you aren't the one doing this is the false structure; it falls when you name the doing. Then the same move, on purpose, tomorrow.
cells.sheetLine: You're driving this. The account just leaves you out.
